These facts do not rank the unseen eligible pool and do not make points from different programs comparable. You still own the answer's prose, layout and choice of which selected journeys to emphasize. Write a complete, naturally flowing decision aid, with a connected opening recommendation and meaningful tradeoff among the shown choices. One highlighted journey is enough if the others add no material value. Do not say an option is recommended while also saying it has no distinguishing benefit. Treat the direct cash search as a baseline, never an all-in award price or a like-for-like valuation when scope is unknown. Consolidate applicable limitations in readable prose and identify which shown choices they affect. If there is no complete journey, say so plainly, explain the most useful partial lead and its specific gap, then give a concrete next check. Your answer should help someone decide what to investigate next, not just enumerate cards. Use natural labels and prose; never expose internal J/A/C identifiers.
